content.p: The Moran family was for more than a decade the best-known name in Melbourne's underworld. A 2010 Canberra Times article called them gunmen, drug dealers and knucklemen, and the family's losses over roughly ten years were heavy. Four of its men were shot dead between 2000 and 2009. In 2011 the family's matriarch, Judy Moran, was found guilty of murdering her brother-in-law, Des "Tuppence" Moran, in a busy Ascot Vale shopping strip.
content.h2: A third generation of Melbourne crooks
content.p: A 2010 Canberra Times retrospective described the family as a third generation of Melbourne criminals, reputed gunmen, drug dealers and knucklemen, whose names were known along the waterfront and at the races. Judy Moran's first husband, Leslie John Cole, was a gambler and standover man, according to the Law Gazette. The Age's timeline dates his shooting to 10 November 1982, outside his Sydney home. She began a relationship with Lewis Moran in 1966 and later changed her name to Moran by deed poll.

Her son Mark was the child of her first marriage. Jason was the son she had with Lewis Moran. Lewis was arrested in October 2002 and accused of trafficking commercial quantities of amphetamine, hashish, ecstasy and pseudoephedrine. He was on $1 million bail when he died. His close friend Graham "The Munster" Kinniburgh was gunned down in front of his Kew home in December, a few months before Lewis's own death, The Age's 2004 report says.
content.h2: The Gangitano killing and the shooting of Carl Williams
content.p: The gangland war is usually traced to 1998. Alphonse Gangitano, a figure linked to the Carlton Crew, was shot dead at his home on 16 January 1998. No one was charged. A coroner believed Jason Moran and Graham Kinniburgh had been in the home that night, the SBS reported in 2015. The Sydney Morning Herald wrote in 2003 that Jason Moran had "almost certainly" killed Gangitano, although no one was charged over it.

The Canberra Times places the start of the bloodshed in October 1999. On 13 October that year, Carl Williams's 29th birthday, the Morans met him in a public park in Gladstone Park. The Morans said they owned a pill press and that Williams owed them $400,000, which Williams denied. According to the Canberra Times, Mark Moran urged his half-brother to kill Williams, but Jason Moran had said they needed Williams alive to get their money. Jason then fired a pistol and hit Williams in the stomach. Williams's wife, Roberta, later said in a conversation that Mark had been yelling for Jason to shoot Williams in the head, and that Jason had then shot him in the stomach.

Williams survived, and the Canberra Times wrote that he then set out to kill every real or imagined rival. Police said he was linked to 10 murders. He was arrested in November 1999 after police searched a house in Broadmeadows and found a pill press and nearly seven kilograms of speed, and a court later delayed his drug cases while two drug squad detectives faced their own prosecutions. The State Library of Victoria's Ergo site gives a different account of the first shot, saying Williams was shot "allegedly by either Mark or Jason Moran". The reports do not settle which brother fired.

Mark Moran was shot dead outside his home in Aberfeldie on 15 June 2000. SBS reported that Williams was charged with his murder but never convicted of it. Three years later, on 21 June 2003, Jason Moran and Pasquale Barbaro were shot dead in a van while the Auskick football clinic at Essendon North was finishing. Five children were nearby, among them Jason Moran's twins. The Sydney Morning Herald wrote that Jason Moran loved football and regularly took children, including his own, to the clinic.

Lewis Moran was shot at the Brunswick club in the early evening of 31 March 2004. His friend Herbert Wrout was wounded in the same attack. Assistant Commissioner Simon Overland told The Age that Lewis Moran had refused police protection, and the paper reported that police had earlier feared for his life while he was on bail. The Age counted his death as the 24th underworld victim in the feud.

Twelve days after Lewis Moran's death, Judy Moran told the Sydney Morning Herald she had signed with the agent Harry M Miller to write a book about her family. She said she wanted to clear her partner's name, and that he had been called a drug baron, which she denied. The paper noted that Victorian law bars people from profiting from stories about crimes they were convicted of, and that she was exempt because she had never been convicted or charged in relation to the family's alleged activities at that point.

Williams was later convicted of ordering the murders of Jason Moran and others. SBS had earlier noted that he was charged, but not convicted, over Mark Moran's death. SBS's timeline gives his sentence as 35 years for three murders, those of Lewis Moran, Jason Moran and Mark Mallia, with the date 7 May 2007. The Law Gazette, writing in 2011, said he had pleaded guilty to a series of killings and received a life sentence. Those two accounts differ on the form of the sentence, and the SBS figure is given here with that difference noted.

Williams died in Barwon Prison, near Geelong, on 19 April 2010, according to SBS. He had been injured in an altercation with another inmate, and SBS reported that he was allegedly struck about the head. The Canberra Times said the death raised questions about the prison system, and raised the possibility that other prisoners believed he had promised to reveal information about an underworld murder.

Desmond "Tuppence" Moran was Lewis Moran's brother. On 17 March 2009 a masked gunman ambushed his car as he sat in it in the driveway of his home in Langs Road, Ascot Vale. The bullet hit the steering wheel, and the driver was lucky to survive, according to The Age. Police made no arrests. The Age quoted the head of the Purana taskforce, Detective Inspector Bernie Edwards, as saying the shot was not a scare tactic.

Three months later, on 15 June 2009, Des Moran was shot at the Ascot Pasta and Deli Cafe on Union Road. Foreign Policy reported that he was shot a number of times at close range, and the Canberra Times, citing the trial, said he was shot seven times. Two men fled in a dark blue or green car. The Age recorded Judy Moran at the scene that afternoon, where police allowed her through the barricades to see the body.

Police told a court that officers saw Judy Moran dumping the getaway car, according to Foreign Policy. The Age reported that she was arrested at 9.35pm that evening while walking home after allegedly ditching the car. A search of her home in Moonee Ponds later found a hidden safe containing three handguns, clothing matching the description of the killer's, a mask and two stolen registration plates. The Australian reported that Judy Moran and a 45-year-old woman, believed to be Suzanne Kane, the sister-in-law of Jason Moran, had been charged with being accessories after the fact. It also reported that Geoffrey Armour had been arrested in Portland, in south-west Victoria, and remanded in court there.

On 17 June 2009 Deputy Chief Magistrate Jelena Popovic refused bail to Judy Moran and Suzanne Kane, saying their access to guns made them a danger to the community. On the evening of 16 June a suspicious fire broke out at Judy Moran's home, causing $150,000 in damage according to The Age. Foreign Policy also reported that police described the fire as suspicious. On 20 July 2009 the charges against Judy Moran, Suzanne Kane and Michael Farrugia were upgraded to murder, according to The Age's timeline.

Armour pleaded guilty to Des Moran's murder in January 2011, as Judy Moran's trial began. Michael Farrugia had pleaded guilty to manslaughter in November 2010 and agreed to testify against his co-accused. He told the court that after the shooting Judy Moran congratulated Armour and patted him on the back as she drove them from the scene. The Age reported his evidence that she then told them to take off their clothes and other items, including the gun, so she could "get rid of everything". Farrugia said he had been told the trip was for a debt-collection job, and that he had not expected a gun.

The defence said Judy Moran had been at Fawkner Cemetery, at her son Mark's grave, on the day of the killing. The Age reported that the jury rejected that account and was satisfied she had driven Armour and Farrugia to and from the cafe. Judy Moran said she was innocent. The verdict came on 9 March 2011, after seven days of deliberation, in a Supreme Court trial of four weeks before Justice Lex Lasry.

Suzanne Kane had pleaded guilty to being an accessory after the fact in January 2011, and in February 2011 she was sentenced to two years, suspended for two years. Farrugia was sentenced in December 2010 to four years, with a minimum of two.

Judy Moran was sentenced in August 2011. Justice Lasry told the court that the jury had not believed her sworn denial of involvement, and he called the killing brutal. He said the evidence showed that Des Moran had been shot seven times and was defenceless at the time. He said Judy Moran had bought Armour a car and believed Des Moran owed her money, and that the killing was committed for financial gain and instigated by her.

Justice Lasry also said that until the killings she had been a person of good character, and that he found it hard to understand why she had become involved in such activity given that her son Mark, her son Jason and her former partner Lewis had all been killed in the gangland wars. He imposed 26 years' jail with a minimum of 21 years before parole. He said the sentence would have been longer but for her ill health and age. At 66 she had arthritis in both knees and a degenerative hip condition on one side. When she was sentenced she said: "Sir, you are wrong. I am innocent." Armour was also sentenced to 26 years with a minimum of 21, and the judge said that if he had not pleaded guilty he would have faced 30 years with a minimum of 25.

The death toll of the feud is reported in different ways. The Age's 2004 coverage counted Lewis Moran's killing as the 24th underworld death, and the Sydney Morning Herald in 2003 said as many as 15 underworld killings in Melbourne in five years had gone unsolved. The State Library of Victoria put the gangland war at 27 deaths between 1998 and 2006. Foreign Policy, in 2009, said the feud had led to the deaths of more than 30 people, and the Law Gazette put the count at somewhere in the region of 30. Each figure depends on which killings are counted, and the reports do not say which list they used.

The account of who fired on Carl Williams in 1999 also differs, as does the account of Alphonse Gangitano's killing. SBS, citing a Herald Sun report in 2015, said that Herbert Wrout had confessed before his death to giving Lewis Moran the gun later used on Gangitano, and that Wrout claimed it was Mark Moran, not Jason, who went to the home. That is an unverified account of a private confession. SBS also reported that no one was charged over Gangitano's death.
Judy Moran's age was given as 64 in 2009 and 66 in 2011. The Age and Foreign Policy gave Des Moran's age as 60 and 61 respectively. Each figure is given with the outlet that reported it.
